title: Trade game MVP: one resource that is also the fuel, loops on the irregular grid's dual graph, and a market war against one rival
description:
Build the minimum playable version of the trade game, to find out whether routing plus a market war is fun. The design was settled in a grilling session; the full record is the obsidian note `Notes/Trading Game Design.md` and the one-page design `Notes/Trading Game One-Page Design.html` next to it. Theme is a lens only (vampires carrying blood); this ticket builds mechanics with placeholder art.

Core rules:
- One traded resource (blood) that is also the wagons' fuel, plus gold. Blood is produced only at bases, at a gold harvest cost per unit, up to a per-lap cap.
- One turn is one lap: the player edits loops, presses End lap, every wagon runs its loop once, each city clears its market, upkeep is paid.
- The map is the dual of the irregular quad grid (cell to cell). Most cells are farmland or villages; cities are the markets. Some regions are impassable (a moor) and a river is crossed only at bridges. The level starts with a road network that winds through villages (not shortest paths), roads kept apart except where they meet. Travel costs 1 blood per cell on-road and 2 off-road; routes between cities are A* over that.
- Loops are knots built with the three existing tools: Pipe (start A→B→A from home; join two loops by cutting one segment in each and bridging the four ends), Grow (highlights the cities that can be added without a self-crossing or crossing another of your loops; over-fuel targets show red with the deficit; each shows +N cells), Collapse (join the ends of a chain of knots into a higher knot). No tool may create a self-crossing. Your loops may touch but not cross; rival loops may cross yours; shared roads draw as parallel lanes, each left of its direction of travel, with arrow lines; an out-and-back road shows two lanes with opposite arrows. Roads are Bezier curves through cell centres.
- Wagons: capacity (fuel plus cargo in one number), buy price, upkeep. A loop can carry several wagons; each runs the knot's full top-level loop and refills at any of the player's bases. A loop whose fuel exceeds its wagon's capacity cannot be committed.
- Stations (gold to buy, gold upkeep per lap) are where a wagon may sell. Bases are a separate building that produces blood and needs the player to be the dominant seller in that city for 2 laps.
- Cost per unit is per loop: (harvest × (burned + sold) + station and wagon upkeep) ÷ sold. Selling more on the same loop makes every unit cheaper. A city's +N cells is shown as the marginal change to its loop's cost.
- Markets: each city needs a fixed D units per lap. Sellers are ranked by their cost per unit; the cheapest fill D first; the price is the cost of the last seller needed, capped at the town's ceiling. Wagons sell automatically at the best prices around the loop while keeping fuel to get home. Unmet demand shrinks the town's population (D shrinks) and raises next lap's price ceiling.
- Price war: a per-city toggle (Off / At cost / 50% below cost) that puts the player first in that city's sell order at that price.
- One rival with a fixed network on the far side of the river; information about it is visible only in cities where both sell (share, price, exact cost; its gold as healthy / strained / distressed).
- Winning: per city, bronze = largest seller, silver = rival second and losing gold, gold = rival withdraws. A level is won at 60% of all demand (unit share) or by bankrupting the rival within the lap limit. Bankrupt = gold below zero for 3 laps, the same rule for both sides.
- Levels: three short solo tutorials (A→B→A start; Grow and fuel limits; Pipe/Collapse and stations) with medal thresholds on gold earned, then the rival level: home plus a profitable three-city loop and one wagon, gold for about two stations, about 20 laps.

UI: a top bar (gold, gold per lap, lap N / limit, home production, a market-share bar with the 60% goal marked); a city menu on click (demand, share pie, price, your loop's cost, and rival info in contested cities, the price-war toggle, upgrade station, build base with its lock reason); a loop list (each loop's fill bar burned / sold / spare, wagon count, cost per unit, buy wagon); a toolbar (Pipe, Grow, Collapse, undo; map modes Network / Owner colour / Market size; whose network is on top; End lap). End lap animates the wagons around their loops with gold rising from each city they sell in.

Not in this ticket: road building and road grades, storage tanks and relays, speed upgrades, espionage, a rival that expands, new rivals spawning in starved cities, contracts, save/load, real art and audio.
definition-of-done:
1. Start New Game opens the trade game on a level built on the irregular quad grid's dual graph: cities, villages, an impassable moor, a river with bridges and a winding starting road network, all deterministic for a level's seed.
2. Routes between cities are A* on the dual graph at 1 per cell on-road and 2 off-road, drawn as Bezier curves through cell centres; off-road stretches are dashed; every segment is labelled with its cost in cells.
3. Pipe, Grow and Collapse build and edit the player's loops through the knot hierarchy, never creating a self-crossing or crossing another of the player's loops; Grow highlights only valid targets with their +N cells, over-fuel targets in red with the deficit.
4. Loops draw as lanes left of their direction of travel with arrow lines, so shared roads and out-and-back roads show one lane per direction.
5. End lap runs every wagon around its loop once, settles each city's market by merit order on each seller's per-loop cost per unit, pays harvest and upkeep, and animates wagons and gold.
6. Stations, bases (gated on 2 laps of dominance), wagons, the per-city price-war toggle, unmet-demand shrinkage, bankruptcy (3 laps below zero) and the 60% share win condition all work as described.
7. One rival with a fixed network competes in the rival level; its information shows only in cities where both sell.
8. The top bar, city menu, loop list, toolbar and map modes (network, owner colour, market size) are drawn and usable with the mouse.
9. Three tutorial levels and the rival level are playable from start to a win or loss screen, with medal thresholds on the tutorials.
10. Unit tests cover dual-graph A* costs, the per-loop cost formula, merit-order clearing (normal and price war), unmet-demand shrinkage and the win/bankruptcy rules.
11. A launch.json entry opens the rival level, and screenshots under tmp/ show the map with loops, the city menu open on a contested city and the end-of-lap result.
testing-plan:
1. Unit tests: A* on a small hand-built dual graph returns the expected path and cost with road and off-road edges and a blocked cell; the per-loop cost formula matches hand-worked numbers; merit-order clearing ranks sellers, sets the price from the last seller needed and caps it at the ceiling; the price-war toggle puts the player first; unmet demand shrinks D and raises the ceiling; bankruptcy after 3 laps below zero; the 60% share win.
2. Run the rival level with ixdar-cli launch and screenshot the opening map; click a contested city and screenshot the menu; End lap a few times and screenshot the settled result.
3. Play each tutorial to its win screen and confirm the medals.
4. mvn -q compile is clean (checkstyle included).
unknowns: Whether the existing Knot pipe/collapse code can carry grid route costs through its distance matrix, or the loop model needs its own cost lookup
How the rival level's numbers (harvest, upkeep, capacities, demand) balance so a price war is winnable but not trivial
changes-made: Market price is the cost of the cheapest seller left with blood unsold (else the town's ceiling), not the cost of the last seller needed: under the latter a lone seller always sold at its own cost and never profited.
Knot's pipe, grow and collapse now clear match slots by segment identity (Knot.removeMatchSegment), so an out-and-back loop's two segments between the same two cities are told apart.
Route undo/redo replays the operation list from fresh singleton knots instead of the per-record undo; the old headquarters picker is gone because each level sets home.
review-summary: TradeScene is now a playable campaign on the irregular grid's dual graph, where Knot loops carry blood that is both fuel and cargo and a rival competes by merit order. It is the minimum game that shows whether routing plus a market war is fun.
